You're helping build a thorough understanding of a repo for its front-end dev lead. This is "Zimmermann" — a client website-redesign/handover project built on the "Agentic Design Workflow" (ADW) template. It produces a framework-agnostic Web Components library (custom element prefix "zimm") extracted from Figma, targeting web + react stacks downstream.

Repo root: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann-Handover

Your scope is ONLY `02-design/library/` and `02-design/catalog/`. Read these thoroughly (full file contents, not just excerpts):

1. `02-design/library/tokens.md` — token documentation (colours, typography, spacing, motion).
2. `02-design/library/common.css` — token CSS custom properties referenced by all component CSS.
3. `02-design/library/elements/` — currently 8 components: add-to-wishlist, button, footer, icon, logo, nav-item, navigation, product-card. Each folder should contain a `[prefix]-[name].js` custom element, a `demo.html`, and an `assets/` folder. Read the actual `.js` source and `demo.html` for EVERY one of the 8 — don't sample a subset. Note shared conventions (base class/pattern, how attributes/slots are declared, how they compose child elements) and any component that deviates from the pattern.
4. `02-design/library/contract/` — `[prefix]-contract.js` (machine-readable API spec per component: tier, attributes, slots, composes, a11y — generated by the `/extract` skill, not hand-edited), `validate.mjs` (static validator for atomic-model rules), `README.md` (how to read/implement from the contract).
5. `02-design/catalog/index.html` — the browsable component catalog shell. It's supposed to read the contract dynamically (no build step) and render live demos grouped by tier with usage snippets and attribute references.

Important background: a recent commit message says "feat: sync 5-tier atomic model update from DDP Design OS template" — figure out concretely what the 5 tiers are and how tier is recorded/enforced (check `_shared/atomic-model.md` at `.claude/skills/_shared/atomic-model.md` if you need the rule definitions referenced by the contract — it's read explicitly by `/extract`, `/deploy-catalog`, and `/handover`, so it's fair game background reading even though it's outside your primary folder scope).

Report back (this feeds into a larger consolidated report, so use clear headers, be thorough but organized, no fluff):
- **Tokens**: what categories exist in tokens.md/common.css, roughly how many of each, naming convention.
- **Tier model**: the 5 tiers, definitions, and how each of the 8 existing components is classified.
- **Custom element pattern**: the shared authoring convention across components, illustrated with one concrete example (pick the most representative component and show/describe its actual code structure).
- **Contract schema**: exact shape of a contract entry (fields present), and what `validate.mjs` actually checks (walk its logic, don't guess).
- **Catalog architecture**: how `catalog/index.html` discovers and renders components from the contract.
- **Anomalies**: anything inconsistent — a component whose contract entry doesn't match its actual `.js` file, broken references, components missing a demo.html or assets, tier misclassifications, etc.

This is a read-only research task — do not modify any files. Keep the final report focused and skimmable; use bullet points and short code excerpts only where they clarify a pattern, not full file dumps.

1	# Component contract
2	
3	The contract is the single source of truth for the component API. Every component
4	that exists (its name, tier, attributes, slots, composition, and accessibility
5	requirements) is recorded here. If it is not in the contract, it does not exist.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## What is in this folder
10	
11	| File | What it is |
12	|---|---|
13	| `[prefix]-contract.js` | The contract: an array of component definitions. Generated and maintained by `/extract`. |
14	| `validate.mjs` | Checks the atomic model rules against the contract. Run before any handover. |
15	
16	---
17	
18	## How to read a contract entry
19	
20	```js
21	{
22	  name:      "Button",          // PascalCase component name
23	  prefix:    "ds",              // tag namespace (from project.config.js)
24	  element:   "ds-button",       // the custom element tag
25	  atomic:    "atom",            // atom | molecule | organism
26	  composes:  [],                // elements this component renders in its own template
27	  attributes: [
28	    { name: "variant", type: "enum",    values: ["primary","secondary","ghost"], default: "primary" },
29	    { name: "size",    type: "enum",    values: ["sm","md","lg"],                default: "md" },
30	    { name: "disabled",type: "boolean",                                          default: false },
31	  ],
32	  slots: [
33	    { name: "default", description: "Button label text" },
34	  ],
35	  a11y:      "role=button, aria-disabled when disabled, keyboard: Enter and Space activate",
36	  status:    "final",           // draft | in-review | final
37	  extracted: "2026-07-07",
38	}
39	```
40	
41	**`atomic`**: the component's tier, determined by what it renders in its own template:
42	- `atom`: renders no other component. `composes: []`.
43	- `molecule`: renders only atoms.
44	- `organism`: renders at least one molecule.
45	
46	`template` and `page` are not valid contract tiers. They are layout-layer deliverables, not Custom Elements. See atomic model Rule F in `.claude/skills/_shared/atomic-model.md`.
47	
48	**`composes`**: what the component's own template renders. Slotted children are not listed here (see atomic model Rule B). This determines the tier and build order: build atoms first, then molecules, then organisms.
49	
50	**`attributes`**: the component's public API. These map directly to `observedAttributes` in the Custom Element. Types:
51	- `enum`: a fixed set of values. Use the `default` if none is passed or the value is unrecognised.
52	- `boolean`: present = true, absent = false.

# Component contract

The contract is the single source of truth for the component API. Every component
that exists (its name, tier, attributes, slots, composition, and accessibility
requirements) is recorded here. If it is not in the contract, it does not exist.

---

## What is in this folder

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `[prefix]-contract.js` | The contract: an array of component definitions. Generated and maintained by `/extract`. |
| `validate.mjs` | Checks the atomic model rules against the contract. Run before any handover. |

---

## How to read a contract entry

```js
{
  name:      "Button",          // PascalCase component name
  prefix:    "ds",              // tag namespace (from project.config.js)
  element:   "ds-button",       // the custom element tag
  atomic:    "atom",            // atom | molecule | organism
  composes:  [],                // elements this component renders in its own template
  attributes: [
    { name: "variant", type: "enum",    values: ["primary","secondary","ghost"], default: "primary" },
    { name: "size",    type: "enum",    values: ["sm","md","lg"],                default: "md" },
    { name: "disabled",type: "boolean",                                          default: false },
  ],
  slots: [
    { name: "default", description: "Button label text" },
  ],
  a11y:      "role=button, aria-disabled when disabled, keyboard: Enter and Space activate",
  status:    "final",           // draft | in-review | final
  extracted: "2026-07-07",
}
```

**`atomic`**: the component's tier, determined by what it renders in its own template:
- `atom`: renders no other component. `composes: []`.
- `molecule`: renders only atoms.
- `organism`: renders at least one molecule.

`template` and `page` are not valid contract tiers. They are layout-layer deliverables, not Custom Elements. See atomic model Rule F in `.claude/skills/_shared/atomic-model.md`.

**`composes`**: what the component's own template renders. Slotted children are not listed here (see atomic model Rule B). This determines the tier and build order: build atoms first, then molecules, then organisms.

**`attributes`**: the component's public API. These map directly to `observedAttributes` in the Custom Element. Types:
- `enum`: a fixed set of values. Use the `default` if none is passed or the value is unrecognised.
- `boolean`: present = true, absent = false.
- `string`: freeform content.

**`slots`**: named `"default"` is the element's child content. Named slots use `slot="[name]"` on a child element.

---

## How to implement a component

1. Read the contract entry for your component.
2. Build one Custom Element per entry. The `element` value is the tag to register.
3. `composes` → your imports. Build those components first.
4. `attributes` → your `observedAttributes` array and prop defaults.
5. `slots` → your shadow DOM slot elements.
6. `a11y` → bake in. Assert in tests.
7. All styles reference CSS custom properties from `02-design/library/common.css`.
   No hardcoded values.

## Definition of done (per component)

- One Custom Element matching the contract API
- All `observedAttributes` match the contract `attributes` list
- All slots match the contract `slots` list
- `composes` matches what the template actually renders
- No props or imports beyond the contract entry
- Light and dark themes verified
- `node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` passes with no violations

---

## Adding a new component

If a design needs a component not in the contract, **stop and flag it** as a proposed
addition. Do not invent a component, attribute, or token outside the contract. Raising
it means agreeing on the API, classifying the tier, extracting it via `/extract`, and
adding the entry here.

---

## Running the validator

```sh
node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs
```

Checks contract integrity and scans all `demo.html` files for unknown element tags.
Exit 0 = clean. Exit 1 = violations listed.

content.text: # Zimmermann Design Library & Catalog — Research Report Scope: `02-design/library/` and `02-design/catalog/` (plus `.claude/skills/_shared/atomic-model.md` for tier-rule background). Read-only; no files modified. Validated key claims by actually running `node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` and cross-checking file paths on disk. --- ## Tokens `02-design/library/tokens.md` (human-readable) + `02-design/library/common.css` (implementation, `:root` custom properties + `.zimm-text-*` typography classes). Prefix on every variable: `--zimm-*`. Schema version 1, sourced from a single Figma file (`MCP-Test--Don-t-Use`), extracted 2026-07-08. | Category | Count | Naming pattern | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | Colour — Greys | 10 | `--zimm-color-grey-{black,900,800,700,600,500,300,200,100,white}` | No `grey-400` — scale jumps 500→300 (flagged in tokens.md itself) | | Colour — Ivory | 4 | `--zimm-color-ivory-{100,200,300,400}` | | | Colour — Status | 4 | `--zimm-color-{coral,green,orange,red}-500` | | | Colour — Opacity | 4 | `--zimm-color-opacity-{15,30,40,50}` | All rgba(25,25,25,x) — grey/900 base | | Colour — Alias/semantic | ~15 | `--zimm-color-{text,bg,border,action}-*` | Text/bg-inverse variants exist in common.css but aren't documented in tokens.md (see Anomalies) | | Typography — primitives | 13 | `--zimm-font-{size,lineheight,letterspacing,weight}-*` | Futura Round (licensed, no CDN — consumer must supply `@font-face`) + Source Serif 4 (Google Fonts) | | Typography — named styles | 21 | `.zimm-text-{h1,h1-strong,h2-strong,h3-strong,label,caption,link-lg,link-sm,btn-lg,btn-sm,product-name,nav,serif,price,footer,body1,body1-strong,body2,body2-strong,mobile-body1,mobile-body1-strong,mobile-body2}` | | | Spacing — scale | 8 | `--zimm-scale-{200,300,400,500,600,800,1000,1200}` (4px grid) | tokens.md only documents 4 of the 8 that exist in common.css (200/500/800/1000) — the file has more (300/400/600/1200) than the doc describes | | Spacing — action sizing | 5 | `--zimm-size-action-*` | height-lg/md, padding-h-lg/md, gap | | Border width | 1 | `--zimm-border-width-default` (1px) | Inferred, not a named Figma token | | Icon sizes | 3 | `--zimm-icon-size-{lg,md,sm}` = 20/16/12px | | | Border radius, shadows, motion, z-index, grid/breakpoints | 0 | — | Explicitly "not found" placeholders in tokens.md | Token candidates table (6 rows) flags un-tokenized hardcoded values from the 07-08 batch (product-card 440px/288px, button 80px min-width, link/footer letter-spacing). **Not updated** for the 07-10 batch — see Anomalies. --- ## Tier model (5 tiers) Defined in `.claude/skills/_shared/atomic-model.md`. Only 3 of the 5 are ever recorded in the contract; the other 2 are spec-layer only (Rule F): | Tier | Definition | Contract-eligible? | |---|---|---| | **Atom** | Renders no other component (markup + CSS + tokens only) | Yes | | **Molecule** | Renders only atoms | Yes | | **Organism** | Renders ≥1 molecule | Yes | | **Template** | Skeletal page frame, named regions, no real content, renders ≥1 organism | No — spec-layer only | | **Page** | Template instance with real content | No — spec-layer only | Key subsidiary rules: icons are attribute values not composed components (Rule A); slotted content doesn't raise tier (Rule B); tier is decided purely by what a component's own template renders, recorded as `composes: []`. **Classification of the 8 existing components** (confirmed by running `validate.mjs`: *"Contract: 8 components (5 atoms, 3 molecules, 0 organisms)"*, exit 0, zero violations): | Component | Tier | Composes | |---|---|---| | Icon | atom | — | | Logo | atom | — | | AddToWishlist | atom | — | | Button | atom | — (note: Figma frame is named "ZIM-Molecules-Button" but renders no sub-components → correctly atom per the rules; contract already documents this) | | NavItem | atom | — | | Navigation | **molecule** | `zimm-icon`, `zimm-nav-item` (both atoms → valid) | | Footer | **molecule** | `zimm-logo`, `zimm-icon` (both atoms → valid) | | ProductCard | **molecule** | `zimm-button`, `zimm-add-to-wishlist`, `zimm-icon` (all atoms → valid) | No organisms yet. Navigation and Footer both carry a `note` flagging that the **designer's intent is organism**, pending introduction of a `zimm-nav-group` / `zimm-subscribe` + `zimm-footer-links` molecule respectively — today's molecule classification is technically correct under the rules, but is a known interim state, not final. (See Anomalies re: this flag not actually being surfaced by the validator.) --- ## Custom element pattern No shared base class, mixin, or imported helper — every component is an independent `class Zimm[Name] extends HTMLElement` following the same shape: ```js class ZimmX extends HTMLElement { static get observedAttributes() { return [...]; } constructor() { super(); this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' }); } connectedCallback() { this._render(); } attributeChangedCallback() { this._render(); } _render() { this.shadowRoot.innerHTML = ``; } } customElements.define('zimm-x', ZimmX); ``` Attributes **are** the state — there's no cached instance state; every render re-reads `getAttribute`/`hasAttribute` and fully replaces `shadowRoot.innerHTML`. All styling references `common.css` custom properties exclusively (no hardcoded colors/fonts found in any of the 8; a handful of un-tokenized pixel dimensions remain, tracked as "token candidates"). **Representative example — `zimm-button`** (`02-design/library/elements/button/zimm-button.js`): reads `variant`/`size`/`label`/`disabled`, branches CSS via two booleans (`p = variant==='primary'`, `lg = size==='large'`), maps directly onto `--zimm-size-action-height-{lg,md}`, `--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-{default,hover,pressed,disabled,focused}` etc., and renders a single native `
